thread:
maya: Heads-up — I opened a small Terraform PR that tweaks the provisioner scaling buffer and adds a secret rotation hook. Noticed some pods failing post-rotate when nodes scale down.
rahul: linking the PR?
maya: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/312 — changes: `karpenter_provisioner.scale_down_deadline_seconds = 300` -> 600, and a `null_resource` that triggers a K8s secret refresh via external-exec.
sam: quick q: are we triggering a rollout of the controllers when the secret rotates? If the controller can't read the new key during scale-down it might fail finalizers.
maya: right now the hook runs `kubectl -n infra patch secret app-credentials --patch ...` then `kubectl rollout restart deployment/ingress-controller`. But the node drain and pod eviction happen concurrently with the Karpenter termination hook, so race condition possible.
jen: could we instead make rotation write both old+new versions to the secret and have a short dual-read window? many apps can accept that for 5-10m.
rahul: dual-key approach is safer. Another option: add a pre-drain lifecycle hook that re-checks secret readiness before `kubelet` SIGTERM. Karpenter supports `lifecycle` but it's a bit heavier.
infra-bot: Deploy pipeline CI results for PR #312: terraform plan OK, e2e cluster tests failed (2/12) — failures around auth webhook timeouts.
sam: those timeouts smell like kube-apiserver under pressure during scale events. Can we throttle the concurrent drains? Karpenter has `consolidation` and `ttlSecondsAfterEmpty` but we want to slow scale-down not scale-up.
maya: I tried increasing `scaleDownDelay` in the provisioner but that didn't apply cleanly via Terraform due to upstream provider bug. PR includes a provider pin to v0.8.3 which fixes the field.
jen: if provider upgrade is in the PR, add a CHANGES.md note. Also add a fallback: in the K8s manifest we can annotate critical pods with `controller.kubernetes.io/pod-deletion-cost` to bias which pods are removed first.
rahul: good call. For autoscalers — HPA is fine, VPA is disabled in prod for our inference nodes, but we should check any legacy VPA objects. Could they be interfering with eviction priorities?
sam: VPA would be weird since it's node-level cpu/mem recommendations. But check the `vpa-admission-controller` logs in the namespace — I've seen weird eviction annotations get injected.
maya: action items I have: 1) update PR to write dual-key secret during rotation, 2) add provider pin + CHANGES.md, 3) add pod-deletion-cost annotations for critical infra pods, 4) add a short pre-drain check in the termination hook.
jen: I'll review the CHANGES.md and help with the pod annotations.
rahul: I'll take the termination hook change — we can add a simple curl to the secret endpoint and retry 5x with 5s backoff before proceeding. Keep it opt-in by a provisioner flag.
maya: thanks — assigning reviewers: @rahul @jen @sam. I also put a note in the PR description about rolling back provider if plan changes look risky.
infra-bot: @maya tag reminder — please add test plan steps: one for rotation during steady state and one for rotation when scale-down is in progress.
maya: done, added two smoke tests and a stress test matrix (scale-down while rotating). CI will run the smoke tests; stress is manual on staging.
sam: one more ask: update our runbook snippet under `/runbooks/autoscaling.md` with a quick checklist to abort secret rotation if scale-down spikes.
maya: will do. If there are no objections I'll merge mid-day after rahul's termination-hook patch. :thumbsup:
jen: :thumbsup:
rahul: LGTM pending minor nits 
maya: merging after fixes, thanks everyone!
